name: Avocado
baseMeaning: A halved avocado, signaling millennial-coded wellness, basic-coded affection, or avocado appreciation.
tldr: 🥑 means avocado, but in chats it also jokes about wellness habits and offers playfully basic affection.

contextMeanings.meaning: The emoji names avocado or highlights the amount of it in a meal.
contextMeanings.example: i'm bringing avocado toast to lunch 🥑

contextMeanings.meaning: It can describe a wellness-focused identity built around simple, healthy foods.
contextMeanings.example: my whole personality is avocado toast 🥑

contextMeanings.meaning: It jokes about trying to appear healthy, disciplined, or well put together.
contextMeanings.example: living my healthiest lifestyle: toast and vibes 🥑

contextMeanings.meaning: It can express playful affection for someone with simple tastes, though it is not automatically romantic.

platformNotes.note: It appears in food videos and captions that lean into wellness routines or avocado-heavy meals. It also works as a knowing wink when an ordinary brunch is presented as an aspirational lifestyle.
In captions and photo posts, 🥑 often identifies the meal or compliments an avocado-centered dish. It can also decorate brunch posts with the familiar wellness and simple-affection joke.
In a private chat, it commonly follows a food update or a casual comment about tastes. Alongside an affectionate message, it can add lightweight warmth without making the exchange overtly romantic.
It is less likely to carry the full social joke in a workplace channel, so it may simply refer to lunch. In a casual team chat, it can join food plans or gently parody wellness talk.

generationalNotes.note: Millennials are most likely to connect 🥑 with wellness routines and the affectionate joke about simple, uncomplicated tastes.
Gen Z may treat 🥑 as deliberately basic or ironic, especially when it accompanies a polished brunch post or wellness routine.
People may take 🥑 more literally unless the conversation establishes the wellness or affection joke.

warnings.title: Taking the joke literally
warnings.description: Someone may think you are only discussing avocado when 🥑 is doing social work. Name the food directly if the conversation needs clarity.

warnings.title: Overreading the affection
warnings.description: 🥑 can suggest playful fondness for simple tastes without indicating romance. Do not treat it as a declaration of romantic interest unless the surrounding message says so.

seoDescription: What does 🥑 mean? It can name avocado, joke about wellness culture, or offer playful, deliberately basic affection depending on the conversation.

longForm.overview:
🥑 entered the emoji set in Unicode 13.0 as the picture of a halved avocado: green flesh, dark skin, and a round pit. Its original job was honest. It sat beside 🍎, 🍌, and 🍓 among the food emoji and could stand for the fruit itself, just as those neighboring emoji could stand for their foods. Before it became a personality marker, a person sending 🥑 could simply be talking about avocado, avocado toast, or what is in the fridge.

The familiar social meaning grew from that plain food identity. For millennials, 🥑 became shorthand for wellness routines, healthy lunches, and the performance of having a carefully assembled lifestyle. It also carries a deliberately ordinary, sometimes self-aware flavor of affection: the sort of “you are basic and I like that” warmth attached to simple tastes and uncomplicated crushes. That does not make every 🥑 romantic. It can praise the fruit, celebrate a food trend, or make the sender seem health-conscious without anyone discussing health at all. The mistake is to treat one fixed interpretation as automatic; context does most of the work.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🥑 usually appears when food is the subject: “I finally made decent avocado toast,” “this sushi place has way too much avocado,” or a caption about lunch. In those chats, it can simply name the ingredient, especially when several words would say the same thing.

In social conversations, it can stand for a mood. A friend may use it to praise a basic brunch spot, mock an elaborate wellness routine, or add affectionate warmth to someone they consider uncomplicated. The fruit has become linked both to wellness aspiration and deliberately plain tastes. Among people who share that joke, 🥑 can feel more pointed than a generic heart.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
🥑 can misfire when someone takes it literally although the sender is joking about wellness, taste, or affection. Outside a group that shares the joke, it may prompt a puzzled question about avocado. Among frequent users of wellness jokes, it can also sound like a claim to be healthier and more disciplined, making the playfulness feel performative.

Do not use it when discussing allergies or dietary restrictions; those details need plain words. Avoid it in formal emails or announcements, where it looks like a personal aside. If you mean avocado, name the dish or send the photo. If you mean “you are basic and I love that,” say that directly. Dry or ironic messages also benefit from words over a food emoji.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🥑 after talking about toast, lunch, or sushi, answer on the food itself: recommend the place, joke about the avocado, or reply with another ingredient emoji. Matching the literal subject is usually more natural than treating a food reference as hidden symbolism.

When the avocado is doing social work, play along with “very on brand,” send 🥑 back, or say “healthier than me and I respect it.” If your message collected 🥑, interpret it against the conversation: after a food photo it is approval; after a wellness boast it may be teasing. A direct “what did you mean?” sounds severe, so “is this the toast one or the wellness one?” keeps the joke open.

faqs.question: What does 🥑 mean from a guy
faqs.answer: It can simply mean the sender likes avocado, but it may also be playful affection or a joke about simple tastes. It does not prove romantic interest without the surrounding message.

faqs.question: Is 🥑 flirty
faqs.answer: Sometimes. 🥑 can accompany affectionate comments about someone being basic or uncomplicated, but it is equally common in ordinary food and wellness conversations.

faqs.question: What does 🥑 mean on TikTok
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it often appears with avocado meals, wellness routines, and ironic brunch content. A creator may use it to signal healthy eating or to tease how basic and carefully styled the food is.

faqs.question: Does 🥑 always mean someone is healthy
faqs.answer: No. It can be literal, affectionate, or ironic, and in some contexts it is used precisely to parody wellness culture rather than endorse it.

conversationExamples.message: i'm basic but you're still my favorite 🥑
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is playful, deliberately simple affection and may carry a little romantic interest. Respond warmly without treating 🥑 as a formal declaration.

conversationExamples.message: i finally made avocado toast that didn't look tragic 🥑
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here the emoji is mostly literal, celebrating the food and the sender’s small achievement. Ask for the recipe or joke about how much avocado went on it.

conversationExamples.message: team lunch is sandwiches and avocado 🥑
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a straightforward reference to the catering menu. Confirm dietary needs if that matters rather than interpreting the emoji as workplace banter.

conversationExamples.message: grandma says avocado is the only sensible breakfast 🥑
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji supports a family joke about uncomplicated food. A simple laugh or agreement fits better than explaining the emoji’s social meaning.

conversationExamples.message: posting my very balanced brunch before it disappears 🥑
conversationExamples.interpretation: The caption combines literal food posting with an ironic wellness pose. Reply with a teasing comment about the suspiciously healthy meal.
